$comment: Trusted receiver signer policy, read from the PR base ref only. Evidence must carry a GitHub artifact attestation produced by exactly this pinned, privileged workflow identity, triggered from exactly this source ref (gh attestation verify --signer-workflow --predicate-type --source-ref). check_signer() additionally recomputes the subject digest itself, checks the signer's own certificate sourceRepositoryDigest against approvedSignerSourceDigests, and compares the signed predicate's own definitionSha256/assessedChecks/expectedPredicate fields -- a bare verify exit code is never treated as sufficient. This authenticates that the exact CI assessment recorded by receiver-attest.yml (structural integrity + factory allowlist + capability revocation + independent execution boundary, see assess_canonical) was produced and approved by that pinned workflow AT an approved revision -- not that a local agent's execution or any particular SLSA security level is retroactively certified.
approvedSignerSourceDigestsBootstrap: Deliberately empty (fail-closed): this receiver must never trust a signer revision it has not actually reviewed, and revision trust can never be read from the evidence/predicate itself -- only from the Fulcio/sigstore certificate's own sourceRepositoryDigest field, which the signed content cannot forge. This is a pre-selected-and-reviewed allowlist, never trust-on-first-use: approval must precede that revision ever signing anything, not follow from observing what a first successful run happened to produce. Bootstrap sequence (manual, explicitly authorized, NOT part of this commit): (1) identify the EXACT commit intended to become the signer revision and review its full diff of receiver-attest.yml (and anything it transitively trusts) against the last-approved revision, if any, BEFORE that commit is ever allowed to run against real evidence; (2) in a dedicated receiver-policy commit, add that specific commit's SHA to approvedSignerSourceDigests and land it on 'examples/enterprise-receiver' so it is reachable before the signer commit is ever exercised for real; (3) only once the approved digest already exists in this file does the first real signing run occur -- check_signer() then verifies the certificate's sourceRepositoryDigest against an allowlist that was populated in advance, never retroactively. Do not force every unrelated future commit on that ref to rotate this list -- only commits that actually change receiver-attest.yml's trusted behavior need a new, separately-reviewed approved digest, and old digests may be retired once no evidence depends on them.
